description: 12 tasks performed purely via the agent-native capability layer: one manifest fetch, then structured HTTP calls per task. No browser involved.

discovery.notes: One-time capability discovery, amortized across all 12 tasks.

T3.notes: Correct in one call, no need to page through the event list.

T4.notes: Booking id returned directly in the response body.

T5.notes: Id already known from T4's response, no lookup call needed.

T8.notes: 1st call returned structured {error: 'not enough seats available'} with HTTP 400 -- no page to re-navigate, just re-call with corrected seats. 2nd call succeeded as booking #3.

T9.notes: 1st DELETE succeeded. 2nd DELETE correctly returned {error: 'already cancelled'} with HTTP 400 -- unlike the DOM UI, the API happily accepts the malformed request and hands back a diagnosable reason.

T10.notes: PATCH on the cancelled booking correctly returned {error: 'booking not active'} with HTTP 400.

T11.notes: FINDING: unlike the DOM route, /api/capabilities/compare has no 'at least 2 ids' validation. The 1-id call returned HTTP 200 with a 1-item array and no error field -- the agent has to notice the array length itself rather than being told. 2nd call (2 ids) succeeded: Improv for Beginners ($20) cheaper. This is a real gap in the capability layer's input validation, not fixed post-hoc so the benchmark stays honest.
